draft.title: Laws and social cohesion
card: Social cohesion means people in a society live together peacefully and trust that others will follow the same rules.
Laws set out how people must behave and what they can expect from others. They protect each person's rights, such as safety and property.
The legal system, which includes parliament, police and courts, makes laws, applies them and resolves disputes when they are broken.
Individuals play a part too. When most people obey the law and use the legal system to settle disputes, society stays stable.
draft.remember: A stable society needs three things working together: people, laws and the legal system.

a.q: Which statement best describes how laws help social cohesion?
opts: They set shared rules and protect each person's rights
They remove all disagreements between people in society
They treat every person in exactly the same way
They let the government control how people behave
a.why: Laws give people shared rules and protect their rights, so they can trust each other and live together peacefully. Laws do not remove all disagreements. They give a way to settle disputes when they happen.
a.clue: Think about what people can rely on when everyone follows the same rules.

b.q: Neighbours in a Ballarat street dispute a fence. Instead of fighting, they take the matter to a court, which makes a decision they both accept. How does this support social cohesion?
opts: Individuals used the legal system to settle it peacefully
The decision stopped any further disputes in the street
Laws alone settled the dispute without the neighbours
The neighbours' rights were set aside for the sake of peace
b.why: The neighbours chose to use the legal system, and the court applied the law to resolve the dispute without conflict. A decision does not mean disputes never happen again. Laws do not settle things alone, because individuals must choose to use the system.
b.clue: Look at what the neighbours did and what the court did.

a.best: They set shared rules and protect each person's rights

b.best: Individuals used the legal system to settle it peacefully

problems.detail: "resolves disputes when they are broken" is muddled: 'they' grammatically refers to laws, and it suggests disputes arise only when laws are broken. Many civil disputes, such as the fence dispute in question b, need not involve a broken law.
